messages:
auto-incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-api queue growth detected (us-west-2). backlog=34912, p95=8.4s, p99=21.6s, error_rate=11.8%. Autoscaler state=PAUSED. Runbook: <https://redwood/runbooks/hosted-queue-spike>

anya: ack. paging primary oncall @raj and infra @mike. severity: potential customer impact, starting triage.

raj: i'm oncall — looking now. can someone drop the graphs (p95/p99, backlog over time, GPU util)?

mike: GPU pools (hosted-gpu-*-usw2) at 98–100% for last ~12m. autoscaler controller logs show repeated create errors from cloud: `quotaExceeded` and intermittent `429 Instance launch rate exceeded`.

sara: who is affected? product impact? javier any customer reports?

javier: multiple customers reporting 504s and slow responses. top affected tenants: tenant-emu, tenant-labs, tenant-commerce. traffic pattern: sudden burst from a marketing campaign + smaller RTUs. Billing events spiking.

raj: running quick checks. pulling provisioner logs:
```
$ kubectl logs -n infra provisioner-0 | tail -n 200
2026-03-15T22:10:12Z ERROR provisioner: createInstance failed: quotaExceeded: Requested 16 GPUs, available 0
2026-03-15T22:10:13Z WARN  provisioner: retrying in backoff
2026-03-15T22:11:01Z ERROR cloud: launch API returned 429: Instance launch rate exceeded
2026-03-15T22:11:42Z INFO  provisioner: scale decision: add 8 nodes -> attempted launches=3 -> stuck
```

mike: confirmed. cloud account hit accelerator quota and also a per-minute instance launch throttle. we can't create new nodes until provider lifts rate limit or quota is raised. i just opened a support case.

anya: ok immediate mitigations we should consider (order of ops):
- divert high-value tenants to Dedicated pools where capacity is reserved
- enable model fallback for low-priority tenants (7B variant) to reduce GPU memory per request
- apply short-term global rate limit for anonymous/public routes (reduce fanout)
- evict large-batch low-priority jobs (if any)
- escalate cloud quota + request burst increase

raj: will execute diversions now. @mike can you share redwoodctl commands to move routing for a tenant?

mike: use `redwoodctl routing update --tenant tenant-emu --pool dedicated-usw2-1`
trying for tenant-emu now...

raj: applied routing update for tenant-emu and tenant-commerce. initial check: their p95 dropped from ~9s to 0.6s. :thumbsup:

javier: great — push comms to those account teams (AP info). i'll prepare status page note: "Partial routing to Dedicated for impacted tenants; mitigation in progress."

mike: attempted manual scale with `redwoodctl infra scale --pool hosted-gpu-usw2 --count 8` but cloud API returned:
```
ERROR: launch failed: quotaExceeded: GPU quota (nvidia_v100) 0/32 available
```
so manual scale blocked.

anya: can we temporarily throttle new public traffic? we should reduce fresh fanout to avoid queue building while we sort provisioning. who can flip the rate-limit?

raj: i can flip a rate-limit rule. applying `burst-control` policy to 50rps per tenant and global 1000rps cap for 10m window.

raj: `admin.policy.apply --name burst-control --rules "tenant:50rps,global:1000rps" --ttl 10m` -> patch applied. logs show immediate reduction in ingress QPS. backlog down to 21,322 (was 34,912). p95 trending down to 5.1s.

sara: good. i'll start handoff notes. taking lead from here for next 2hrs to coordinate with cloud and product. cc @mike for infra.

mike: update from cloud support: case CS-2026-8791 opened. provider acknowledges rate-limit and suggests ETA 25–40m for launch allowance; they also suggest we request quota increase which takes longer (< 24h). They temporarily elevated launch rate by small burst (allowed +4 instance launches). Ticket: https://cloud.case/CS-2026-8791

javier: product question: do we have an expected ETA to restore normal routing for all tenants? we need an ETA for status updates.

raj: given current provider ETA, estimate partial recovery in 30–45m assuming we can launch enough instances incrementally. full catch-up depends on backlog drain rate.

anya: interim customer impact summary for comms:
- visible symptoms: 504/timeout spikes, elevated p95/p99 for hosted API
- scale: backlog peaked ~35k requests; currently ~21k and falling after rate limit and routing diversions
- affected: subset of hosted customers (the ones on low-priority default routing); paying customers moved to Dedicated see normal latency
- mitigation actions: tenant routing diversions, temporary global rate-limit, model fallback enabled for low-priority routes, cloud SLA escalation.

mike: we also found autoscaler bug causing it to pause on repeated 429s rather than backoff/retry with jitter. opened PR to change behavior to exponential backoff + continue scaling for partial successes. will push hotfix after containment.

raj: manual workaround in the meantime: increase `provisioner.max_launch_in_flight` to 12 to batch the few allowed launches when provider permits. editing config now.

raj: config change applied. next launch batch succeeded for 4 nodes at 22:18Z (provider allowed burst). GPU pool capacity +4, utilization down to 94%. backlog down ~6k.

auto-incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: backlog=15210, p95=3.2s, p99=9.8s, error_rate=6.2% (22:20Z).

javier: product comms draft ready. i'll publish a status update in 10m after we confirm sustained fall in p99.

anya: longer-term followups (to capture in postmortem):
- autoscaler robustness for API rate limits (don't PAUSE on 429s)
- pre-authorize higher accelerator quotas for peak/shielded accounts
- refine routing fallback automation to auto-divert top X tenants when backlog > threshold
- add synthetic checks to detect sudden fanouts and pre-warm pools

raj: handoff: sara will lead till 00:30Z then i'll take night shift. tagging PD schedule. please update the incident doc and add timeline + logs (I saved provisioner logs to /infra/incidents/1772222222/).

sara: noted. i'll keep watch and post if p99 climbs or cloud support updates. leaving detailed notes in the incident tracker. thanks all for quick moves.

mike: cloud support acknowledged our config change and allowed additional launches; ticket updated: CS-2026-8791. asked them to confirm if accelerator quota increase is accepted; ETA unknown.

auto-incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigation in progress — reduced customer impact. severity -> S2 (was S1). next automated metric push in 5m.

anya: closing loop for now. remaining action items documented. will follow up with postmortem to include queryable graphs and exact timeline. :white_check_mark:"
